# M78 read-only revisit2 preparation

## Verdict

The revisit2 adapter is prepared as source-only work. It has not executed a recovery, restart, authentication, hosted request, database operation, provider action, or revisit. Broader board authorization for the read-only preservation sequence persists, while the two technical admission dependencies remain unavailable: an independently accepted actual recovery2 receipt and an independently verified same-image restart receipt.

The earlier blocked revisit adapter and the accepted recovery2 runner/evaluator remain unchanged. Revisit2 uses new exclusive evidence and lock paths and cannot write to either predecessor run.

## Admission contract

An accepted recovery2 bundle must rerun the frozen full evaluator and return `m78_independent_continuation4_readonly_recovery2_passed`. Its separately pinned independent receipt must identify `/root/m78_transport_probe`, have zero open findings, say that the actual recovery is accepted, retain zero application POSTs and closed sessions, and bind the exact journal, diagnostics, raw capture, observation, source gate and `Recovery2ReviewAdmission`. That evaluator result does not itself authorize restart or revisit.

The restart chain consists of separately hashed admission, request, provider acknowledgment, startup and independent review documents. It permits exactly one deployment restart and zero revisit application POSTs. The request reason is `scope1_persistence_verification`; the provider acknowledgment is exactly `{data:{deploymentRestart:true}}`. Startup must contain exactly one `staging_started` event after the request and before observation, schema 21 readiness, legacy containment, and `autodeploy:false`. Every item binds commit `9dd9c85fb674528a2c1dd1b0138f5a2d87ba683e`, deployment `f6d77b2e-6886-429b-a4d2-4873c9199ce8`, and image `sha256:3e4c2c91591a5598a85f63b4099b1b4890588ce79ec832b21b7d284b5aa89d1b`.

The chronology is strict: accepted recovery2 closure precedes the restart request, which precedes the sole provider startup, which is no later than startup observation. This is an explicit deployment restart for persistence verification. Automatic deployments being disabled is not treated as provider autopause or resume evidence.

A distinct fresh recovery2-compatible source gate must include `m78-readonly-revisit2.ts`, bind the same fixed runtime, and differ from the source gate used by the accepted recovery. The frozen recovery2 runner then performs its own complete pre-authentication source and historical-evidence checks.

## Exclusive execution boundary

The adapter verifies and preserves the failed first recovery journal, diagnostics and durable lock, plus all four accepted recovery2 artifacts and its durable lock. The failed first recovery observation remains absent. Every revisit2 output must be absent before entry and a separately pinned revisit2 lock must already be held.

The unchanged recovery2 runner receives an IO adapter that maps only its journal, diagnostics, raw-capture and observation paths to the four revisit2 paths. Any other read or append is refused. Fetch, authentication, expected subjects, legacy reader, admission, decoders and clock pass through unchanged. The inherited runner remains GET-only for application traffic, uses local logout, has no retry path, and cannot claim success after incomplete cleanup or diagnostic failure.

After the inherited runner reports a closed zero-write pass, the adapter constructs a fresh `Recovery2ReviewAdmission` from the revisit2 bytes and reruns the frozen full evaluator. It then compares the fresh observation's `scope1`, seven `registers`, `downloads`, `m78bytes`, five `fullReports`, and `legacy` exactly with the accepted recovery2 observation. It also requires ten Scope 1 sources and company total `126850.17632025`. Timestamps and observation-run metadata are outside the retained-state comparison.

The only adapter success status is `m78_readonly_revisit2_passed`. It does not authorize another restart or revisit.

## Offline validation and remaining gates

Six focused tests passed with 105 assertions, and strict targeted TypeScript passed. The tests cover all four remapped paths, immutable predecessor evidence, exact pass-through dependencies, unavailable or altered actual receipts, wrong runtime/image, wrong restart purpose, negative provider acknowledgment, multiple startup events, open review findings, chronology, used paths, missing or wrong locks, each changed retained-state family, inherited runner failure, and unsupported IO.

The structural positive injects the runner and evaluator and uses synthetic pinned receipts. It proves the adapter contract only. It is not an actual recovery, restart, transport capture, production-decoder acceptance, or hosted revisit. Root owns the fresh source gate, private wrapper, physical locks, actual recovery2 execution, restart and any later revisit. Independent source review of the exact frozen candidate remains required.
